entries.title: UK AISI/CAISI: Kimi K3 Safeguards Failed Offensive Cyber Tests — Open-Weight Release (2.8T, Largest Ever) Proceeds Tonight
entries.summary: A joint UK AISI/CAISI evaluation found Kimi K3 scored 32% on the Carnegie Mellon ExploitBench versus ~76% for leading US models, reached only step 17 of a 32-step simulated network attack, and — critically — its safeguards did not prevent it from attempting exploit development or offensive cyber operations; the 2.8-trillion-parameter model (1.4 TB in MXFP4, the largest open-weight release in history) proceeds to public release at 00:00 UTC July 27 regardless, making model-level safety filters irretrievable post-release.

entries.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 5: 85% Fewer Safety Classifier Triggers, New Silent Fallback Feature, Billed as 'Most Aligned Model'
entries.summary: Anthropic released Opus 5 on July 24 with safety classifiers expected to engage 85% less frequently than Fable 5 (by design: Anthropic deliberately withheld advanced cybersecurity training to lower the risk profile), a new opt-in 'Automatic Fallbacks' feature that silently routes flagged API prompts to a less capable model instead of returning an error, and no 30-day data retention requirement — a distinct compliance profile that creates governance questions about which model tier is actually governing sensitive deployments.

links.title: Anthropic Opus 5 Launch Advances AI Performance and Safety (Cryptonomist)

entries.title: 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership': 50-Company Coalition Urges Washington Against Restrictions — Anthropic and Amazon Absent
entries.summary: Jensen Huang used his first-ever X post (July 24) to launch a 25-company letter arguing that restricting open-weight AI would weaken US leadership; the list doubled to 50 by July 25 and OpenAI later signed, but Anthropic and Amazon (Anthropic's largest investor) remained absent, crystallizing a public schism over whether Chinese open-weight models should be restricted and who bears the governance risk.

entries.title: EPA Proposes Rule Letting States Eliminate Community Review for AI Data Center Air Permits
entries.summary: The Trump EPA is considering allowing individual states to set their own standards for public participation in minor-source air permitting, the permit class that xAI and Meta use to build gas and diesel generation facilities for AI data centers, which would reduce or eliminate community notification and review rights and materially shift ESG and infrastructure risk for frontier AI build-out.

links.title: EPA Rule Change Would Let States Gut Public Participation in AI Data Center Permitting (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: FSB AI Sound Practices Consultation Closes (July 22); Final Report Due October 2026
entries.summary: The Financial Stability Board's July 22 comment deadline passed on its consultation proposing 12 sound practices for responsible AI adoption by financial institutions — covering board-level governance, full AI lifecycle management, and specific guidance on agentic AI risks — with a final report due October 2026 that will function as a de facto international supervisory checklist.

entries.title: arXiv 2607.21325: Cryptographically Verifiable Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
entries.summary: Submitted July 23, this paper proposes a formal model (CVA) using zero-knowledge proofs to cryptographically bind an AI agent's specific request, its principal, and the applicable policy into a verifiable relation — directly addressing the core authorization gap where agents issue tool calls on the basis of text they cannot verify, with any context-controlling party able to forge apparent authority.

links.title: arXiv 2607.21325: Toward Cryptographically Verifiable Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents

entries.title: IBM Publishes Agentic AI Governance Playbook — Adversarial Testing and Hard Autonomy Boundaries as Pre-Deployment Requirements
entries.summary: IBM's July 25 Agentic AI Governance Playbook advises organizations to define agent purpose, scope, and decision boundaries before development begins, prescribes risk classification, adversarial testing, and explicit approval workflows as pre-deployment requirements, and mandates least-privilege access controls — establishing an industry benchmark for what 'responsible agentic deployment' looks like before regulators formalize it.

links.title: IBM's Agentic AI Governance Playbook Sets an Industry Benchmark (AI Governance Institute)
